{{Article header|deck=A field reference for Stratum Tectonicas, including value, sampling distance, environmental profiles and known visual variants.}}

{{Exobiology species infobox}}

'''Stratum Tectonicas''' is a low-growing Stratum species protected by a thick, rock-like outer shell. A contrasting lattice of brighter cells across the surface performs photosynthesis.<ref name="canonn">[https://us-central1-canonn-api-236217.cloudfunctions.net/query/codex/ref Canonn Codex reference], snapshot retrieved 28 September 2026.</ref>

== Identification ==

In the field, look for broad, flat growths with a stony surface and a brighter irregular cellular lattice. Their low profile can make individual colonies blend into uneven ground when viewed from a shallow angle.

== Variants ==

The named variants below follow the current Codex reference.<ref name="canonn" />

{{#invoke:Exobiology|variants|title=Stratum Tectonicas}}

== Practical notes ==

The 500-metre sampling separation is large enough that travelling by ship or SRV is usually faster than walking between colonies.
